propositions: Parallel multi-session compaction writes corrupt the worktree by mutating files (SNAPSHOT, *.retired renames, .archived deletions) before git commit, leaving dirty state unrecoverable on worker death.

The git merge origin/tickets operation aborts in two variants: untracked files that origin wants to create, and tracked-file deletions/modifications that local changes would overwrite, both stranding commits and breaking plan-review attestations.
Runtime markers (*/.archived, */.write.lock) are committed as tracked files in HEAD before their gitignore patterns existed, causing persistent tracked dirt in routine marker churn.
The compaction fold must become crash-atomic with an intent journal sentinel outside the worktree to enable safe rollback on partial failure and recovery parity for both merge and push operations.
Store-wide scans (fsck, compact-all) must default to active tickets only and accept --include-archived to reach archived tickets, scaling scan cost with the active working set.
The fsck/doctor repair tooling must detect and heal dirty-tree and stale-lock classes (tracked deletions, untracked regenerable leftovers, orphaned locks) under the write lock.
